title: Distributions workload: phit, phit-polyfill, R and SciPy
description: Elapsed time and peak memory to evaluate the normal and gamma CDF and quantile functions over 1,000,000 inputs each, with batch calls, in the phit extension, phit-polyfill, R and SciPy.
workload: Normal CDF and quantile, gamma (shape 2.5, scale 1.5) CDF and quantile, 1,000,000 inputs each

environment.threads: One thread everywhere: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, OMP_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS and BLIS_NUM_THREADS set to 1 for R (OpenBLAS), numpy and GPBoost (OpenMP). phit and phit-polyfill are single-threaded.

method: Each run is a fresh process. Each implementation runs once as a warm-up, then the 4 alternate for 7 rounds in a rotated order. The time runs from the inputs already in memory (a PHP array, an R vector, a numpy array) to holding all four results. Building the inputs is outside the timing. Every process runs under /usr/bin/time -l. Memory is the process's peak memory footprint as macOS reports it, data included: its own allocations, without the clean file pages it maps. peak_rss_mib gives the peak resident set size, which counts those pages. baseline_memory_mib is each runtime's peak footprint with its libraries loaded and no data. No iterations to compare. phit and phit-polyfill use the _array batch functions (cdflib normal and incomplete-gamma backends). R uses its vectorized pnorm, qnorm, pgamma and qgamma. SciPy uses stats.norm and stats.gamma cdf and ppf on numpy arrays.

code.R:
normal_cdf <- pnorm(x)
normal_quantile <- qnorm(p)
gamma_cdf <- pgamma(positive, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.5)
gamma_quantile <- qgamma(p, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.5)
code.SciPy:
normal_cdf = stats.norm.cdf(x)
normal_quantile = stats.norm.ppf(p)
gamma_cdf = stats.gamma.cdf(positive, 2.5, scale=1.5)
gamma_quantile = stats.gamma.ppf(p, 2.5, scale=1.5)
